final.summary: Outfall flow stayed high for over eleven hours while treated flow was normal, with a large excess volume that the tank balance cannot account for. Outfall pH stayed near neutral and conductivity was low during the extra flow, which points to added low-conductivity water rather than untreated wastewater. Because the outfall readings were altered by added water, a human must judge the measurement point tampering.

explanations.label: Normal operation: batch wastewater treated through ETP
Bypass around ETP: untreated water to outfall
Dilution: groundwater added to outfall
Meter fault: outfall or inflow meter error

key_evidence.why: Outfall exceeded treated flow by 232.6 m3 beyond tolerance, with tank unaccounted 200.0 m3, showing extra water left the tank by another route.
Outfall mean 79.4 m3/h versus outside median 55.5 m3/h shows sustained extra flow.
Conductivity mean 5122.6 uS/cm versus outside median 6430.0 uS/cm shows low-conductivity water during extra flow.
pH mean 7.38 max 7.64 stays neutral, ruling out raw wastewater in the extra flow.
Power 69.6 kW matched expected 68.7 kW with zero share outside band, showing aeration ran.
Photo 69.9 kW consistent with feed and within expected band, confirming power feed.
No identical stretch and low correlation rules out replayed power feed.

final.scope_line: Based on flow, power, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 10:00 to 2026-10-14 14:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: Logbook claim of normal operation is a factory claim, not a fact, and is contradicted by the water balance.
Lab sample at 14:35 and power photo at 21:14 are point measurements and do not represent the whole 11.25-hour excess stretch.
Conductivity and pH show the extra flow was not raw wastewater, but do not identify the exact pipe or valve used for dilution.
No outfall flow meter photo or independent flow verification was available to confirm the outfall reading absolutely.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
